questions.question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

Government governed by wealth
questions.solution:
The** correct answer **is 'Option 4' i.e.** 'Plutocracy'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given phrase** 'Government governed by wealth'** refers to a type of government where the rich and wealthy individuals hold the power.(धनशासित सरकार)

 
 
• **Example:** Historical Venice is often cited as an example of a plutocracy, with its wealth-based system of government.
 
 
 
• **Plutocracy** is a form of oligarchy and defines a society ruled or controlled by the small minority of the wealthiest citizens.(समृद्ध वर्ग द्वारा शासित समाज)
 
 
• **Example:** Some critics argue that the United States has become a plutocracy because of the power held by Wall Street and other wealthy interest groups.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is** 'Option 4' i**.e.** 'Plutocracy'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1 '**Theocracy'**: Theocracy is a form of government in which a deity of some type is recognized as the supreme ruling authority, giving divine guidance to human intermediaries that manage the day-to-day affairs of the government.(ईश्वरीय शासन)
 
• Option 2 '**Autocracy': **Autocracy is a system of government in which supreme power is concentrated in the hands of one person, whose decisions are subject to neither external legal restraints nor regularized mechanisms of popular control. (स्वयंशासन).
 
• Option** 3 'Democracy'**: Democracy is a form of government in which the people have the authority to choose their governing legislators.(लोकतंत्र).

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

Most of Earth's surface is covered by water.

options.text: Water is covering most of Earth's surface.
Water has been covering most of Earth's surface.
Water covers most of Earth's surface.
Water has covered most of Earth's surface.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "Option 3:** Water covers most of Earth's surface."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the passive voice:* Object + auxiliary verb + past participle + by + agent.*
 
• In active voice, the structure is: *Subject + Verb + Object.*
 
• **"Water covers most of Earth's surface"** places the doer (water) first, and retains the present simple tense, making it the correct choice.
 
• **'Covered'** will be changed into** 'covers'.**

Therefore, the **correct answer **is - "Option 3: Water covers most of Earth's surface."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Options 1, 2, and 4 incorrectly change the tense from present simple to present continuous, present perfect continuous, and present perfect, respectively.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Pritha will been cooking / the meal of your choice / before you / reach home.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Option 2: Pritha will been cooking".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The segment** "Pritha will been cooking"** contains a grammatical error.
 
• The correct form of future perfect continuous tense is **"Subject + will have been + verb-ing".** 
 
• Therefore, *"Pritha will been cooking" *should be **corrected to** *"Pritha will have been cooking"*.
 
• Furthermore, we use the future perfect continuous tense for actions that will be ongoing until a certain point in the future. This fits the given sentence context.
 
• Lastly, the other segments are grammatically correct and meaningful in the sentence context.

Therefore, the **correct answer** is **"Pritha will have been cooking".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1:** "reach home"** This segment is grammatically correct in this sentence context.
 
• Option 3: **"the meal of your choice" **This segment is grammatically accurate as it properly describes the meal.
 
• Option 4:** "before you"** This segment is accurate and serves to set the time reference for the future perfect continuous tense.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.

__
 
• **"Consume" **is a term often used to depict the utilization of a resource, especially oil, fuel, energy, or food. In this context, it refers to the amount of oil that is being used up by human activity.
 
• So the sentence becomes "Every day we consume 70 million barrels of oil".

Therefore, the correct answer is **"Option 1". **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• "Take" is a very general verb and would technically make sense in this context ("Every day we take 70 million barrels of oil").
 
 
• However, it is less precise compared with "consume". "Take" could imply a simple act of possession rather than usage.
 
 
 
• "Absorb" is usually used to describe a process where one thing becomes incorporated into another thing, usually in a passive manner.
 
 
• This term is not typically used when referring to the usage of resources like oil.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"was founded". **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Was founded"** is in the simple past passive voice, which makes sense in this context.
 
• This option fits perfectly as it shows the action done by an unknown (or unimportant in this context) entity in past.
 
• It states that in 1924, the company "Total" was established by someone.

Therefore, the correct answer is **"Option 2". **

 
• **So, the correct sentence would be:** "Total was founded in 1924, and for many years it was a French state oil company. In 1999, Total joined Petrofina, the Belgian oil and gas company, and in 2000, Total merged with its main French competitor, Elf Aquitaine, and the name became Total Fina Elf. Now it's called Total again, and it's France's biggest company."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "Had founded" is in the past perfect tense and usually refers to an action that occurred before another past action.
 
 
• Here, it does not work because there is no other past action to reference.
 
 
 
• "Founded" on its own doesn't provide the necessary auxiliary verb (was or were) to signify passive voice in the past.
 
• "Were founded" is incorrect because "Total" is a singular noun and "were" is used with plural nouns.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"merged". **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Merged" **refers to when two or more entities become a single entity.
 
• In our case, it could mean Total and Elf Aquitaine becoming one company.
 
• This term is frequently used when two companies combine to form one.
 
• Thus, the sentence should read: "In 2000, Total merged with its main French competitor, Elf Aquitaine, and the name became Total Fina Elf."

Therefore, the correct answer is **"Option 1". **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "Combine" is typically used in a more general sense when two or more things are mixed together, but in a business context, it lacks the precision and connotation of two separate entities coming together to form a single one.
 
• "Join" usually refers to becoming part of a group, team, or organization, and lacks the connotation that two separate entities become a new, single entity, which the context suggests.
 
• "Incorporate" is typically used to refer to including something as part of something else, and it doesn't quite capture the meaning in this context.
